request.system: You are a sceptical results reviewer. Task: rank Medicare providers for audit. Each of 5,410 providers carries a PotentialFraud label (9.35% flagged) whose origin is undocumented; treat it as suspicion, not confirmed fraud. Claims run 27 Nov 2008 to 31 Dec 2009. The primary metric is PR-AUC; the audit queue holds about 100 providers. Pick the configuration to carry forward. Prefer a simpler model unless a more complex one is better by more than one standard deviation of PR-AUC across folds. Flag any result that looks too good. You may request up to 2 more round(s) of experiments; set stop=true if further search is unlikely to help. Rate your confidence in chosen_run (0-1): 1.0 means results are clear-cut and no reasonable reviewer would disagree; 0.5 means the top configs are too close to call or something looks off. (Independent run 1.)

concerns: Fold SDs of PR-AUC (0.056-0.079) are larger than every gap between configs. The best (run 3, 0.7328) beats the simplest (run 1, 0.6809) by 0.052, below one SD (0.0595 for run 1, 0.056 for run 3), so the simpler-model rule favors logistic.
Run 2 (RF) beats logistic by only 0.024 and run 3 beats RF by 0.028, both well inside one SD. The ranking among the top configs is not reliably separated.

The PotentialFraud label has undocumented origin, so it is only suspicion. High ROC-AUC (~0.94) with PR-AUC ~0.7 may partly reflect the labeling rule echoing volume or size features rather than real fraud.

Run 3 uses agent features (all+agent) with no size removal, and the gain from them is unclear. Size features may act as a proxy for volume and leak labeling logic; the no_size logistic reaching 0.68 suggests the signal is not just size.
Only 4 configs tried, with confounded changes (model, feature set, imbalance all varied together), so attribution of gains is impossible.
Precision@50 is 0.74-0.78 across all configs, a small spread. The queue is ~100 providers, so P@100 is not reported and top-of-list quality at the actual audit depth is unverified.
No sign of an implausibly good result: PR-AUC 0.68-0.73 is plausible, but the high ROC-AUC with moderate PR-AUC at 9.35% prevalence deserves a leakage check on the label and feature construction.

next_experiments.rationale: Isolates the effect of agent features on the simple model, so the benefit of agent features can be separated from model complexity.
Same as run 3 but without size and agent features, to test whether the LightGBM gain comes from the model or the feature set, and whether size acts as a proxy.
A more regularized variant of the best config to check whether the gain is robust and whether a smaller model matches it with lower fold variance.
